extracted.intended_audience: poets and literary critics; writers interested in poetic craft and the principles of literary criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing poetry and for performing literary criticism: principles of tone, accuracy, balance, classical models, and the personal virtues a critic should have. Focuses on how critics ought to judge and how poets ought to write.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrain censure; prefer silence to spite
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Tis best sometimes your censure to restrain, And charitably let the dull be vain; Your silence there is better than your spite
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not respond angrily to every bad writer; charitable restraint or silence is often the wiser response than harsh public denunciation. Avoid expending energy on malicious attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid perpetual railing; criticism need not endlessly attack
rubrics_metrics.description: For who can rail so long as they can write? Still humming on, their drowsy course they keep, ... False steps but help them to renew the race
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endless fault-finding fuels more bad writing rather than correcting it; recognize that many errors are self-correcting and that prolonged railing is ineffectual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not be a 'bookful blockhead'—avoid pedantry
rubrics_metrics.description: The bookful blockhead ignorantly read, With loads of learned lumber in his head, ... All books he reads and all he reads assails
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading many books does not substitute for taste, judgement, or understanding. Avoid becoming a pedant who parrots authorities without sound judgement or without appreciating true merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced candor: teach without pride, be modestly bold
rubrics_metrics.description: But where's the man who counsel can bestow, Still pleased to teach, and yet not proud to know? ... Modestly bold, and humanly severe, Who to a friend his faults can freely show, And gladly praise the merit of a foe?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good critics counsel and instruct with humility. They are willing to point out faults to friends and to acknowledge merit in rivals; combine firmness with humaneness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact yet unconfined taste; combine book-knowledge with knowledge of mankind
rubrics_metrics.description: Blessed with a taste exact, yet unconfined; A knowledge both of books and human kind; Generous converse, a soul exempt from pride; And love to praise, with reason on his side?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate precise discernment without narrowness; pair learning about literature with insight into human nature; be generous in company and free from vanity; praise when warranted and support it with reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge with coolness; write with fire (be consistent: passion in work, calm in judgement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Horace still charms with graceful negligence, And without method talks us into sense; ... He who supreme in judgment as in wit, Might boldly censure, as he boldly writ, Yet judged with coolness though he sung with fire; His precepts teach but what his works inspire
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emulate Horace: let your writing be lively and passionate but your critical judgements calm and measured. Rules and precepts should be supported by the critic's own exemplary writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid judging with fury while writing with dullness
rubrics_metrics.description: Our critics take a contrary extreme They judge with fury, but they write with phlegm
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allow vitriol in critique if your own prose is lethargic or uninspired; avoid the mismatch of harsh judgment and poor expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in quotations and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nor suffers Horace more in wrong translations By wits than critics in as wrong quotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics must be careful and accurate when quoting or translating sources; misquotation undermines credibility and damages the validity of criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer modest caution over noisy nonsense
rubrics_metrics.description: Distrustful sense with modest caution speaks, It still looks home, and short excursions makes; But rattling nonsense in full volleys breaks, And, never shocked, and never turned aside, Bursts out, resistless, with a thundering tide
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speak cautiously and sensibly; avoid loud, unconsidered assertions (rattling nonsense) that sweep all before them without discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repress license and ordain useful laws (uphold standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Thus long succeeding critics justly reigned, License repressed, and useful laws ordained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism has a role in restraining excesses of taste and in establishing useful norms and standards of literary art; this is a constructive, regulative function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be ardent yet just; let your example strengthen your rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Thee bold Longinus! all the Nine inspire, ... An ardent judge, who, zealous in his trust, With warmth gives sentence, yet is always just: Whose own example strengthens all his laws; And is himself that great sublime he draws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine zeal and passion with fairness and justice; the critic's own work should exemplify and validate the standards he enforces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value classical models but avoid slavish imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The mighty Stagirite first left the shore, Spread all his sails, and durst the deeps explore; ... Horace still charms ... Quintilian's copious work we find The justest rules and clearest method joined:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study classical critics (Aristotle, Horace, Quintilian, Longinus) for rules and methods, but apply them sensibly rather than slavishly; let ancient precepts inform sound judgement rather than become dogma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature and craftsmanship: prize well-written, natural expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Such was the muse, whose rule and practice tell 'Nature's chief masterpiece is writing well.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At root, excellence lies in writing well—natural, well-crafted expression is the highest aim. Craft and naturalness are primary measures of poetic success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Praise when deserved; avoid both flattery and needless offense
rubrics_metrics.description: Careless of censure, nor too fond of fame, Still pleased to praise, yet not afraid to blame, Averse alike to flatter, or offend
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strike a balance: be willing to praise honestly and to blame when necessary, but avoid mere flattery and avoid causing offense without reason.
